A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPHERE research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable matching despite the added analyses and presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original sequential-editing experiments on LLaMA3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, including benchmark results, HE analyses, general-ability evaluations, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements and a hyperparameter sensitivity study in Sections 5.6–5.7.

M1.justification: The principal-space construction, projection matrix, and projected weight update in Equations 10–13 remain unchanged, as does the integration procedure in Appendix D.5. The new sensitivity study varies existing hyperparameters rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CounterFact and ZsRE for editing and GSM8K, RTE, Natural Questions, and BoolQ for general abilities. The added Qwen2.5-32B runtime measurement changes model configuration, without establishing additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FT, MEMIT, PRUNE, RECT, AlphaEdit, and the pre-edited reference. Section 3.1 still includes ROME, and Figure 7 retains MEMIT, PRUNE, and RECT. The new analyses reuse MEMIT without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.6 adds editing-time, projection-time, and timing-ratio measurements for three model configurations, including Qwen2.5-32B, using MEMIT with 3,000 edits and batches of 100. Section 5.7 adds a 4-by-4 eta/alpha sweep on LLaMA3-8B with MEMIT and 3,000 edits. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused checks of computational overhead across three model configurations and sensitivity to the two projection hyperparameters on one model/base-method pair. These supplement the retained HE correlations, weight-geometry analyses, general-ability tests, and appendix case studies.

E5.justification: The existing Table 1 uncertainty entries, Figure 7 error bars, and Figure 3 confidence ellipses and regression analysis are retained. v2 adds no seed or repeated-run disclosure or new uncertainty-estimation procedure; its new displays report point values.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix results are retained. New Table 2 reports projection times of 18.00, 35.95, and 99.60 seconds and corresponding timing ratios of 3.31%, 6.71%, and 6.01%. New Figure 8 reports sensitivity scores ranging from 21.77 to 89.00 with both parameters nonzero, versus 10.63 when either is zero. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under a revised method.

T1.justification: The HE definitions, theoretical bounds, orthonormal-input and small-perturbation assumptions, and Appendix C proofs are unchanged. The new experiments introduce no mathematical definition, theorem, or proof revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the HE–editing-stability connection, the SPHERE projection contribution, and the reported 16.41% main improvement and 38.71% plug-and-play improvement. The added analyses support the existing practical-scalability positioning without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 5.6–5.7 newly interpret the overhead as lightweight and similar across Qwen model scales, and describe broad hyperparameter robustness with application-specific tuning. The latter interpretation needs qualification: Figure 8's zero-parameter controls retain the baseline score despite the text claiming improvement across all configurations.

D1.justification: v2 adds runtime information and a project-website link. It removes the reproducibility statement promising a future code release while retaining the same code-link destination. Appendix D's existing implementation details, including edited layers, optimization steps, learning rates, and hardware, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Li et al.'s Reinforced Lifelong Editing for Language Models changes from a preprint reference to its ICML publication entry, which is a bibliographic update to the same work.

P1.justification: The research-question list expands from four to six, with new Sections 5.6–5.7. v2 also lightly edits the ethics statement, removes the standalone reproducibility statement, and updates acknowledgments and the publication header. The existing scientific narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime Table 2 and sensitivity heatmap Figure 8. Existing figures are retained, with appendix Figures 8–12 renumbered 9–13. The additions cause limited text and page-layout reflow rather than a redesign of the existing displays.

improvement.justification: The runtime measurements and parameter sweep modestly improve assessment of practical cost and sensitivity, which v1 did not explicitly test. Their value is limited because Figure 8 does not identify its dataset or metric, and its zero-projection controls contradict the blanket improvement claim. These focused additions provide useful evidence while leaving the central method, proofs, and benchmark results intact.
